title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers and payload limits; routing rules for OpenAI compatibility and tool-calls
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We continue to see intermittent stream stalls and poorly handled large tool-call payloads when routing through the streaming proxy in multi-tenant/redirect scenarios and when using the OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR contains a set of conservative, backwards-compatible defaults and routing rule improvements to reduce stalls, avoid proxy backpressure amplification, and support larger payloads for structured tool/function-calling responses. Summary of changes: 1) Increase streaming proxy read/write buffer defaults from 64KB -> 256KB and add adaptive buffer growth to cap at 1MB per connection to reduce syscalls and improve throughput for bursty token streams. 2) Increase maximum request payload accepted by the API gateway from 4MB -> 8MB for OpenAI-compat routes and tool-calls; maintain 4MB for user-facing public routes by default. 3) Add route-based payload policy in routes.yaml so teams can opt-in to relaxed limits for dedicated/durable backends. 4) Improve routing decision logic to prefer regional low-latency pools for streaming tool-calls and fall back deterministically to a compatible model variant when capacity constrained (reduces ambiguous 502/504 outcomes). 5) OpenAI compatibility: preserve legacy header behavior for application/x-ndjson streams while enforcing strict content-length and chunking validation on non-compat routes to avoid reassembly bugs. 6) Add additional connection-level metrics (proxy.buffer_size_bytes, proxy.write_backpressure_ms, gateway.route_policy_matched) and hook them into Console dashboards and alerts. 7) Tests: add unit coverage for the adaptive buffer, e2e test for large tool-call payloads using the OpenAI-compat route, and flakiness guard for streaming e2e. Rollout plan: canary deploy to us-west-2 for 48 hours with traffic shifting rules targeting 5% of traffic on dedicated/hosted clusters; monitor proxy.write_backpressure_ms and error rates; automatic rollback trigger if streaming error rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes or p95 latency regression > 15%. Backwards compatibility: All changes are default-preserving for non-opted routes; OpenAI-compat opt-in changes only apply to routes with compatibility flag. No breaking changes expected. Notes on CI: initial integration-e2e had a transient failure in the streaming-resume test (flaky network emulator) which was fixed by adding a jitter to the test harness; final checks passed and load-canary verified no regression under 10k concurrent connections. Related: references ENG-4821 for routing policy work and SUP-9981 for the support case that drove larger payload support.
commits: feat(proxy): adaptive buffer growth with hard cap and defaults bumped to 256KB
feat(routes): route-based payload policy and OpenAI-compat flag
fix(routing): deterministic fallback to compatible model variants under capacity pressure
chore(metrics): add proxy buffer/backpressure metrics and dashboard hooks
test(e2e): large payload tool-call test for openai-compat route; flakiness guard
docs: release notes and rollout checklist
review_comments: Ravi Singh: Can we make the 1MB hard cap configurable via env var? If customers need higher limits we should gate it behind a feature flag.
Aisha Patel: Added GATEWAY_PROXY_BUFFER_CAP_BYTES env var and documented in helm config; default remains 1MB (configurable at deploy time).
Elena Martinez: The route-based payload policy looks good, but please add a short circuit to validate Content-Length for chunked streams to avoid double buffering.
Aisha Patel: Implemented Content-Length/Chunk validation in middleware and added unit tests.
release_notes: Improve streaming proxy stability and increase OpenAI-compat payload limits: default proxy buffers increased and adaptive growth added to reduce stalls; OpenAI-compat routes support up to 8MB payloads; route-based payload policies allow opt-in relaxed limits for dedicated backends. Added metrics and canary rollout plan.
